info.title: COSS API
info.description: One API key for every COSS product. Errors share one envelope: `Error`. Every request is scoped to the environment the key belongs to; domains and the audit log are organization-wide.

CossVersion.description: The API version (a date) to use for this request. Defaults to your organization's version, pinned to the latest one when it first used the API and upgraded from the dashboard. The SDK always sends the version it was built for.

post.description: Queues an email from the API key's environment and returns it with `status: "queued"`; it is handed to the delivery provider moments later. Follow it with `GET /v1/emails/{id}` or the `email.sent` / `email.failed` webhooks. Live (`coss_live_…`) keys must send from a verified domain of the organization. Sandbox (`coss_test_…`) keys accept any `from` and never deliver anything; the response has `sandbox: true`. Recipients on the environment's suppression list (for every email, or for the email's `category`) are skipped and get the status `suppressed`. With a future `scheduled_at` the email is stored with the status `scheduled` and sent at that time; the domain and the suppression list are checked again then. Attachments are base64-encoded; only metadata is kept after sending. Recipients count against the organization's send quota (per second and per day; sandbox environments have their own daily quota). With open or click tracking on (the environment's settings, or `tracking`), the HTML body is delivered with a tracking pixel and/or links rewritten to COSS redirects; the stored `html` stays as sent.

post.description: Queues up to 100 emails in one request. Each email is handled exactly as by `POST /v1/emails` (sender checks, suppressions, scheduling, attachments, tracking), but the batch is all or nothing: if any email is invalid, or any `from` is not a verified domain (live keys), nothing is stored and the error names the email (e.g. `emails.3.to`). One `Idempotency-Key` covers the whole batch. The emails' recipients are charged against the send quota together, so a batch with more recipients than the quota allows at once is refused (`quota_exceeded` without `Retry-After`): split it. The request body shares the 40 MB limit of a single send.
